title: FedLNS: Leverage LayerNorm Signature Modeling to Mitigate Adversarial Manipulation in Federated LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.18736v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Federated training enables language models to learn from distributed private text, but the server cannot directly verify the local supervision or optimization process that produces each client update. A malicious client can therefore train on corrupted targets, introduce incorrect context-token associations, and degrade the global model through repeated aggregation. Such degradation can also increase the risk of unreliable or hallucinatory generation. We propose Federated Learning with Normalization Signatures (FedLNS), a server-side framework for lightweight malicious-update screening. FedLNS represents each client update through changes in trainable normalization-layer parameters and screens suspicious updates against a robust, history-aware cross-client reference. translated_title: FedLNS：利用层归一化签名建模缓解联邦大语言模型中的对抗性操纵
translated_abstract: 联邦训练使语言模型能够从分布式的私有文本中学习，但服务器无法直接验证生成每个客户端更新的本地监督或优化过程。因此，恶意客户端可以基于被破坏的目标进行训练，引入错误的上下文-词元关联，并通过重复聚合降低全局模型的性能。这种退化还可能增加不可靠或幻觉生成的风险。我们提出了带有归一化签名的联邦学习（FedLNS），这是一种服务器端的轻量级恶意更新筛选框架。FedLNS通过可训练归一化层参数的变化来表示每个客户端更新，并针对一个稳健的、基于历史感知的跨客户端参考来筛选可疑更新。由于签名是在服务器端从返回的本地模型中提取的，与现有方法相比，FedLNS不需要额外的客户端到服务器参数或元数据交换。
tldr: 本文提出了FedLNS，一种服务器端轻量级框架，通过利用层归一化签名建模来检测和过滤联邦大语言模型中的恶意客户端更新，无需额外通信开销，从而缓解对抗性操纵并提高模型稳健性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes FedLNS, a server-side lightweight framework that detects and filters malicious client updates in federated large language models by leveraging layer normalization signature modeling, without additional communication overhead, thereby mitigating adversarial manipulation and enhancing model robustness.
